batch_observations: ELEVEN PLAYS, RE-AUDITED UNDER THE CORRECTED RUBRIC AND RE-MEASURED FROM THE FILES RATHER THAN INHERITED. BRAIN_AUDIT_PARTIAL_S111.json already covers all eleven under the old rubric; I re-ran every headline number myself and reached the same arithmetic in every case, with two class changes that the corrected rubric forces and one that it does not. CLASS COUNTS: MECHANISM_VERIFIED 3, OUTCOME_CREDITED 6, NOVEL_N1 1, NOT_A_PLAY 1, ASSERTED 0, UNCLEAR 0. || THE TWO CLASS CHANGES vs S111. (1) structure.squeeze_unwind -> NOT_A_PLAY. Its own call field reads verbatim 'DESCRIPTOR grade - regime context, not a scored play', status DESCRIPTOR, confidence 0.4, forward_evidence NONE, and it explicitly refuses to promote a band. The rubric names this case: NOT_A_PLAY is for DESCRIPTOR-grade regime context. Forcing it into a support class was the same category error the worked lng_export example describes. (2) daytype.friday_crest_trim_discriminator -> NOVEL_N1, up from ASSERTED. Its covering-vs-squaring arm is a real mechanism (price UP into settle AGAINST sell flow = forced covering, not voluntary squaring) and its first instance is traced to an INDEPENDENT channel: research/kalshi/renders/ng_refine_s95/g15_mbo_evidence.json shows 20260327 closing +1160 UP on total_sflow -2,470 with absorb_session true and the final phase the most one-sided sell of the day (-1,878 on 55,181 lots) while price still rose +280. The classification is derived from the flow signature, not from which way the day went. That is the NOVEL_N1 discriminator exactly. || THE THREE THAT ACTUALLY MEASURE SOMETHING. boundary.chain_staleness_gate and tape.heavy_buy_aggression are the only two plays in this batch whose evidence is a re-runnable aggregate over committed files, and BOTH reproduce to the dollar on independent recomputation - chain_staleness_gate additionally forward-confirms on G21-G23, blocks outside its derivation set (k<=3 mean 652 vs k>=4 mean 2041, a 3.1x step in the same place as the derivation set's 793 vs 2432). direction.flow_nowcast is also measurement-shaped, and that is precisely why it is the batch's most serious finding: the measurement DOES NOT REPRODUCE. || THE BATCH'S SINGLE WORST NUMBER. direction.flow_nowcast carries confidence 0.87 - the highest in the batch - on a claimed rate_oos of 1.0 and a monotone RISE with signal strength (0.68 -> 0.84 -> 0.94 -> 0.93). Re-measured on the file the claim was computed from, research/kalshi/renders/ng_refine_s95/fingerprints.json (6,351 usable legs, 108 days, 2025-09-08 to 2026-02-27), the play's own |dip_imb_level| >= 0.15 bar gives 2,459/3,697 = 0.665, and the monotone is INVERTED: 0.688 / 0.665 / 0.628 / 0.575 at bars 0.10 / 0.15 / 0.20 / 0.30. The signal gets WORSE as it gets stronger. Split by era it is 0.876 before 2026-01-19 and 0.515 after - a coin flip - and the play has produced nothing but stand-down text since G17 because dip_imb_level is served in zero modern decision states. || THE STRUCTURAL FINDING WORTH GREG'S TIME, and it is new here. timing.catalyst_continuity_frontrun's central read - 'is a LIVE continuous catalyst present?' - HAS NO SERVED DEFINITION, and the two natural readings of the same served object disagree in SIGN on the same day. On 20260624 the state serves weather_forecast.forecast_run_delta_cdd = -0.011 (horizon 0) and weather_forecast.run_delta[h1].d_gw_cdd = +0.787. Specialist C read the horizon-0 number on 0624 and concluded 'the ramp is not updating' (stood down); six sessions later, on 0630, the same specialist on the same block read the ladder LEVEL and concluded 'a live continuous CDD ramp IS present'. Both days delivered +800 and +780. The condition appears to change state only because the reader picks the quantity. And under the one served reading with a definition, it is DEGENERATE: run_delta h1 d_gw_cdd is positive 20 of 20 across G22+G23 (min +0.129, max +2.256) - the same constancy that killed the burn gate, sitting inside a second play nobody has checked it against. That is D23's disease with a third face: not a value bar and not a transfer failure, but a condition with no served referent at all. || WHAT I COULD NOT SEARCH, AND WHY IT MATTERS. monday.window_deep_book_shakeout is the one play in the batch whose headline rests on a number committed NOWHERE. git grep imb10 returns only knowledge/ng_brain.json, its backups and the S111 audit file. S102_MERGE_PROPOSAL.md restates the 6/7 in prose, which per the instance discipline is one instance, not two. Two of its seven named Mondays (20251027, 20260309) are not even in fingerprints.json, and fingerprints carries a per-LEG imb_R at leg-entry time on L1-3 depth fields, not a Monday 06:00 L1-10 snapshot. That is not_searched, and it is not a failure of mine - it is the finding. || A COUNT THAT SURPRISED ME. Across g22 and g23 the eleven plays of this batch account for 66 explicit invocations in the committed per-day posteriors, and 47 of them are STAND-DOWNS. Three plays stood down on every single appearance (flow_nowcast 6/6, squeeze_unwind 14/14, prior_exit_lasthour 5/5, window_deep_book 4/4 - four, in fact). The modern blind is largely running on the absence of this batch.

audits.the_argument: NG's leg side = sign(dip_imb_level) when |dip_imb_level| >= 0.15, fired on the lagging Kalshi mark. The support is measurement-shaped, not day-net-shaped: n_strong_oos 34 at rate_oos 1.0, a monotone strength gradient stated as 0.68 -> 0.84 -> 0.94 -> 0.93, and an S95 fingerprint pass over G3-G5 held legs. Confidence 0.87, the highest in this batch. It sits in the MECHANISM family because the support IS a measurement and the mechanism (aggressor flow overlaps the nascent leg, so a signed imbalance nowcasts the leg's side) is argued rather than assumed. I classify it here and then report that the measurement does not reproduce - which is a stronger result than any label, and is only available BECAUSE the support was a measurement.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Yes, and it comes out the other way. I re-ran the play's own bar on the file the claim was computed from. Over 6,351 usable legs on 108 days, |dip|>=0.15 gives 2,459/3,697 = 0.665, not 1.0, and the claimed monotone RISE with strength is INVERTED on the corpus: 0.688 (>=0.10) / 0.665 (>=0.15) / 0.628 (>=0.20) / 0.575 (>=0.30). The signal degrades as it strengthens. The rate is also nowhere near 1.0 anywhere, so this is not an overlapping-window tautology artifact - it is a real result, and the era split below is the shape of it. The play's own declared weak day (1020, quoted as 7/12) reproduces honestly at 10/14 on my slice, which is evidence the record is written in good faith even where the headline is wrong.

audits.the_argument: Two claims stacked. (1) Monday is a BIG mover, size UP. (2) The side comes from a three-armed reaction read - FADE a gap that jumped with a mature swing to a fresh cum-extreme, EXTEND at a fresh turn, and with no material gap carry FRIDAY's side. The bigness claim is checkable and I checked it. The three arms are not: every evidence entry in the play is of the form 'date X moved +N, guessed +M' with an arm assigned afterward to explain it, across eight separate per-event blobs (g6, g7, g10, g11, s96_2, s97_2, s98_2, s101_6, s102_1). The arms were carved out of the outcome record rather than derived from an independently measured quantity - the play says so itself when it retires the G3-G5 'Monday reversals' as 'swing-state coincidences, not a weekday property'.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: For the bigness claim yes, and it comes out the other way. For the arms, largely no: with three arms and a free swing-state selector, every Monday lands in one of them by construction. The play does carry two genuine acts of discipline that argue against a blanket dismissal - it FORWARD-FAILED its own gap-size arm in writing (1020, 0118, 0125 all under-forecast), and its declined_evidence block refuses to bank g20 0601's R3 as forward evidence because the constructed chain was inverted there, which is a specialist catching a state defect being laundered into evidence.

audits.the_argument: An armed turn near a scheduled catalyst fires the session BEFORE the event when a continuous weather ramp is live, and waits for the event when it is not. The causal argument is genuine and stated - weather models are a continuous twice-daily information stream, so when live they own the timing and the discrete print only adds magnitude and liquidity. But the core support is a catalogue: '1110 exhausted -> 1111 +1580', '1118 armed -> 1119 +1930', '1203 front-run confirmed +1520', with the fired/waited arm assigned after the fact. There is no independent measurement anywhere in the corpus of the ramp-live condition against a front-run rate. This is the best-behaved OUTCOME_CREDITED play in the batch - it carries two live self-falsifications (G9 1204 forward-failed in its original form and was re-armed; G10 0108 established the forbidden polarity-flip form) - but its support is still a list of days that delivered.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Partly, and the part that could is the good part. The G16 pair is a real discriminator test that traces exactly to the committed price file: 0401 (D-1 to a pre-priced +34 print) delivered -590 and 0402 round-tripped to -150 / day_move -130, against 0409 (not pre-priced, building surplus on the block's most active tape) which delivered -610 with NO round-trip. Had 0409 also round-tripped, the discriminator would have died on the spot. That is real. The core fired-vs-waited tally (n=3 fired, n=2 waited) is not - it is five days sorted into two bins after the outcome.

audits.condition_can_change_state: This is the play's real defect and it is worse than a degenerate bar. The trigger has TWO limbs. The calendar limb (a scheduled catalyst 1-3 sessions ahead, served as flow_calendar.days_to_next_eia_release) is live and splits days cleanly. The ramp-live limb has NO SERVED DEFINITION, and the two natural readings of the same served object disagree in SIGN on the same day (20260624: horizon-0 forecast_run_delta_cdd -0.011 vs h1 d_gw_cdd +0.787). Under the h1 reading it is a constant, positive 20/20 across two groups - it cannot gate. Under the level reading it is whatever the reader says. So the limb either cannot change state or changes state by reader choice, and the corpus contains one specialist doing both inside one block.
audits.falsifier: The play carries NO falsifier field, though its caveats name a decisive test in prose ('the decisive test is the next winter armed-turn near a print'). What it actually needs first is a SERVED DEFINITION of ramp-live - pick the quantity and the bar - because until then the condition is not falsifiable, only arguable. Once defined: front-runs under a live ramp must beat the base rate of the pre-print session, measured on the intraday window and not on the day net (this is the exact defect s103.6 had to retract on D's pre-print generator).

audits.the_argument: This entry is not a conditional rule and says so in its own call field: 'DESCRIPTOR grade - regime context, not a scored play.' status DESCRIPTOR, confidence 0.4, forward_evidence NONE, n=1 full instance self-declared, and it explicitly refuses to promote a band. It is a description of what G12 did after the dead-sponsor squeeze - the unwind retraces the full squeeze leg in two gap-led sessions to the pre-squeeze shelf, then bases - with the magnitudes inside the unwind derived as arithmetic (gap = -E, next session = remaining premium to the shelf). Classifying its support was the category error the corrected rubric was written to stop, so I say what it is and record what traces. WHAT TRACES EXACTLY: the two unwind sessions. WHAT DOES NOT: the nine-session basing band, which is wrong on the upside by 0.291 (about 2,900 dollars in day-move terms).
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Not applicable as a support test - it is a descriptor. But two of its statements are checkable and I checked both: the unwind arithmetic reproduces to the tick, and the basing band does not reproduce at all. The S101.6 amendment is also a genuine act of scoping under pressure rather than tent-widening: when G13 broke the 3.159 shelf three weeks later, the claim was NARROWED to the unwind sessions themselves and the post-basing shelf was demoted to an ordinary reference level, rather than the descriptor being loosened to accommodate the break.

audits.the_argument: A Monday 06:00 ET L1-10 resting-book imbalance (|imb10| >= ~0.05) marks the caught/stacked side, and the 06-10 window leans AGAINST it as a tie-breaker under R3, never overriding it. A mechanism IS argued - Greg's weekend-carry read, modified by measurement to 06:00 rather than the Sunday reopen because the reopen book measured uninformative at 8/14. But the support is 'qualifying 6/7' on a subset selected at a bar chosen by the same refine pass that saw the outcomes: 7 of 14 Mondays were filtered out and the rate is quoted on what survived. On n=7 a 6/7 is roughly p=0.06 one-sided against a coin flip, and the play itself reports that the shallower L1-3 read gives 8/14 and that the window repricing runs against its own aggressor flow 8/14 - both coin flips. The play states its own remaining gap honestly: no Tue-Thu control run, so Monday-specificity is unproven.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: In principle yes, but I cannot put it to any test, because the underlying measurement is committed NOWHERE - so the play's headline cannot have come out the other way in any way anyone can check. THE FULL SEARCH RECORD, since d24_state is not_searched and I list ZERO instances rather than dressing stand-downs up as evidence. (1) git grep imb10 across the whole repo: hits ONLY in knowledge/ng_brain.json, its version backups, and BRAIN_AUDIT_PARTIAL_S111.json - zero hits anywhere in research/kalshi/forecasts/ or research/kalshi/renders/. (2) grep for imb10 and imb_R across research/kalshi/renders/ng_refine_s95/grp20_state.json through grp23_state.json: absent from all four. (3) research/kalshi/renders/ng_refine_s95/fingerprints.json, the only committed file carrying any book quantity at all: it holds a per-LEG imb_R at leg-entry time on L1-3 depth fields (bid_dep_entry / ask_dep_entry), which is the wrong depth AND the wrong timestamp for a Monday 06:00 L1-10 snapshot, and two of the seven named derivation Mondays (20251027, 20260309) are not in it at all. (4) research/kalshi/S102_MERGE_PROPOSAL.md lines 70-73 restate the 6/7, the L1-3 8/14 and the against-own-flow 8/14 in prose only - and per the instance discipline, prose citing prose is one instance, not two. (5) The four modern Mondays in research/kalshi/forecasts/g22_perday/grp22_B_20260622.json, research/kalshi/forecasts/g22_perday/grp22_B_20260629.json, research/kalshi/forecasts/g23_perday/grp23_B_20260706.json and research/kalshi/forecasts/g23_perday/grp23_B_20260713.json: the play is STOOD DOWN on all four with firehose_present.l1_book FALSE in every case, and B on 0622 recorded that the only book it could see was a Friday object which it carried at explicitly zero weight. Those are traceable STAND-DOWNS, not instances of the mechanism, so they are named here and NOT counted.
audits.condition_can_change_state: CANNOT BE CHECKED, and that is the finding. The bar (|imb10| >= ~0.05) sits on a quantity that is served in no modern decision state and committed in no evidence file. The play's own figure implies 7 of 14 Mondays cleared it, which would make it comfortably live - but that number is not auditable from anything in the repo, and firehose_present.l1_book is false on every modern Monday so it cannot even be evaluated forward.
audits.falsifier: The play carries NO falsifier field, but two are named implicitly in its own text and both are writable: (a) a run of qualifying Mondays where the 06-10 window leans WITH the heavy L1-10 side; (b) a Tue-Thu control run showing the same rate, which would kill the Monday-specificity the play admits is unproven. WHAT WOULD SETTLE THIS PLAY: serve imb10 in decision_state at the Monday 06:00 ET snapshot, or archive the L1-10 book for the seven named derivation Mondays, then re-run. Until one of those exists neither falsifier can be run and the headline cannot be checked by anyone.

audits.the_argument: On a mid-week turn day the prior session's last_hour_dir gates MAGNITUDE: an opposing prior exit means the reversal realizes post-open, so size the confirmed base and never front-run the reactive tail; an aligned exit means momentum carries, so do not cap. The headline support is 'n: 6 opposing-exit reversal days (all D-1 lhd<=0) across g9, g10, g12, g15 = a strikingly consistent signature: EVERY clean mid-week reversal-up day in the record had a prior session that exited DOWN.' That is a base-rate artifact and it is the most important finding in this batch after flow_nowcast. The mechanism was inferred from which days delivered, and the word 'clean' does the selecting.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Barely. last_hour_dir is -1 on 25 of 40 modern sessions, and over consecutive within-group pairs the prior exited down on 22 of 36 = 61 percent. A claim of the form 'every reversal-up day had a prior exiting down' on n=6 is close to what six random draws give you. And the structure forecloses disconfirmation: the aligned counter-case (g9 0223) is quoted as its own separate arm, so no observation in the record can fall outside one of the two arms.

audits.the_argument: Adds two discriminators to the crest-trim trigger, which had fired BOTH ways: (1) based-vs-stretched - crest-trim fires only on a STRETCHED chain near a cum-extreme, never a based one; (2) covering-vs-squaring - price UP into settle AGAINST sell flow is COVERING (forced, positioning_spent, do not fade) rather than genuine same-side squaring at a stretched extreme (the trim). I re-read this under the corrected rubric and it is NOT ASSERTED, which is where S111 put it. The covering-vs-squaring arm is a genuine mechanism - forced covering and voluntary squaring are different acts with different flow signatures - and it has a NAMED FIRST INSTANCE traced to an INDEPENDENT measurement channel, not to the outcome. That is NOVEL_N1 by the rubric's own discriminator, and n=1 is not a reason to downgrade it.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: For the covering arm, yes, and this is the load-bearing point. The classification of 20260327 as covering rests on session and phase signed flow from the MBO evidence store, not on the day's sign: the session closed +1160 UP on total_sflow -2,470 with absorb_session true, and the FINAL phase was the most one-sided sell of the day (-1,878 on 55,181 lots) while price still rose +280. Had 0327 closed up on BUY flow, the tell would have said squaring and the discriminator would have been wrong on its own founding day. For the based-vs-stretched arm, no: it carries no numeric bar on any served quantity, so nothing in the corpus can contradict it, and 0710 shows two readers could class the same day either way. One arm is measured, one is unfalsifiable, and I am classing the play on the arm that is measured.

audits.the_argument: The covering-absorption UP tell is not unconditional - its SIGN flips with extension. Young / low-extension absorption of a dip is short-covering UP; maximally extended (cum above about +2000 from the block anchor AND chain age >= 5) with the absorption tell ITSELF reversed is late chasers being absorbed, which is DISTRIBUTION DOWN. The support is 'g19: UP on 0515, DOWN on 0520; the pair is the discriminator; 0519 was AT extension but absorption had not reversed, so correctly NOT flipped'. Three days, one block, and all three readings were produced by the REFINE with the realized price curve in hand. The mechanism - late chasers absorbed equals distribution - was inferred from which way the days went, not tested against anything independent. The play states its own weakness plainly and to its credit: 'n=3 within one block, needs a second block'.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Marginally, within the block: 0519 is a real non-fire at extension and it could have flipped and did not. But the discriminator has three free terms (a cum bar, an age bar, and absorption-reversal) fitted to three days by a refine that knew all three answers. One term per observation is a guaranteed fit. The one component that IS a real measured correction is the assumption_retired block, and it is the best-supported thing in the entry.

audits.the_argument: A deterministic SCHEDULE rather than a signal: a play keyed on cum_from_anchor or chain extension may assert a RUNG only for k <= 3 sessions from the block anchor; from k >= 4 it widens to the full band or stands down. It rests on a single aggregate measurement - mean |constructed cum - realized cum| by k across G17-G20 - plus the structural observation that k is known in advance in a one-shot block blind, so nothing has to be inferred at runtime. It is one of only two plays in this batch whose evidence is a re-runnable aggregate over committed files rather than a narrative of days, and it is the only one that also carries a written forward test with an explicit kill condition.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Yes, decisively, and in two separate ways. A flat divergence profile would have killed it outright. A smooth accumulation would have made the k<=3 boundary arbitrary - independent random-walk accumulation of uncorrelated daily errors predicts only about 1.15x growth at the k=3 to k=4 step, against the 2.13x measured in the derivation set and 1.91x forward. Neither null happened, so the kink is real and is evidence of CORRELATED (block-lean) error rather than mechanical accumulation - which is the play's implicit mechanism and it survives its own null.

audits.the_argument: As merged in S110 the play claimed a CDD slope lean converts to a gas call only if est_gas_burn_bcfd confirms flat-to-up and wind is not ramping against it, reading BOTH ways. Its support was six in-block G22 instances with the arm assigned to each after the day delivered - 0629 wind up 62 percent / burn down 4.2 suppressed a realized CDD add (-1,160); 0624 wind down 22 percent / burn up 6.3 delivered (+800); 0630, 0703, 0625, 0702 as confirming mirrors. Six days, one block, never spanning: the textbook OUTCOME_CREDITED shape. It is now REFUTED_FORWARD_TEST_S110_G23 on its own named forward test, and I audited the RETIREMENT as well as the play, because a retirement can be as badly evidenced as a merge. It is not. It rests on two mechanism arguments and I reproduced both from the served state, plus one test of my own that neither refuter ran.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: The original G22 support, no - six days sorted into two polarities inside one block, and the play's own evidence list contains the pair that kills it. The REFUTATION, yes, decisively: it is a claim about the behaviour of a served series and I re-measured it independently three ways, any of which could have come out the other way. This is the clearest case in the batch of the difference between the two - the merge was outcome-credited and the retirement is mechanism-verified.

audits.condition_can_change_state: NO ON THE LIMB THAT MATTERED, and that is exactly why the play died. The CDD-add limb (d_gw_cdd at h1) is positive 20/20 across two groups - it never changes state, so whatever discriminating work the gate appeared to do in G22 was done by the wind and burn limbs, not by the CDD read. The burn limb DOES change state (flat-to-up on 12 of 18 computable sessions, down on 6) but is anti-predictive in the confirm state. This is the batch's clearest instance of D23's discrimination disease, and it is a RATE property: the limb is a delta, which is the form D23 recommends, and it still cannot gate because the delta is one-signed in the regime.
audits.falsifier: WRITTEN AND DISCHARGED, which makes this the best-documented retirement in the brain - and the falsifier's FORM is still worth flagging. As written ('a burn-confirmed CDD add that fails to deliver, or a wind-on day that delivers gross-CDD anyway, in G23+') it is a SINGLE-INSTANCE falsifier: one day discharges it, and C-0707's single instance the other way cannot un-discharge it. A play whose falsifier fires on n=1 is guaranteed to die on its first forward block regardless of merit. The retirement stands anyway because it never rested on the tally - both killing arguments are mechanism arguments and I reproduced both.

audits.the_argument: Same-day net BUY aggression is a bearish-to-null tell that strengthens monotonically with size (agreement with price 41 / 29 / 25 / 20 percent as the threshold rises through +1000 / +1500 / +2000 / +3000 lots), while the SELL side carries no comparable information (flat at 46 / 43 / 46 / 47), and the same quantity on D-1 is a coin flip so it must never be used as a next-day direction input. The support is a full-corpus aggregate over committed files with per-event listing, a stated base-rate comparison, a DECLARED NEGATIVE CONTROL, a written falsifier, and an honest D24 declaration in its forward field ('CORPUS SEARCHED, INSTANCES FOUND ... all 70 sessions'). Alongside chain_staleness_gate it is one of only two plays in this batch whose evidence is a re-runnable aggregate rather than a narrative of days.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Yes, at four thresholds independently and on both sides of the tape - and it DID come out otherwise on the one arm that decides usability. The D-1 arm is a null (4/9, 6/11) and the play REPORTS the null rather than burying it, then converts the play into a PROHIBITION on the strength of it. That is the opposite of the S108 signature. The one part that is genuinely unsupported is the causal STORY for the asymmetry (persistent offer-side supply from producer hedging, index roll, call overwriting) - that is a plausible reading of the numbers, nothing in the corpus separates it from other explanations, and it is not what the play's instruction depends on.
